pi5_4gb.summary: Quad-core Linux computer that runs ROS 2, perception and the gait planner
pi5_4gb.description: The Raspberry Pi 5 is the high-level brain of Strido. It runs Linux, Docker and ROS 2, reads the LiDAR and camera, and streams joint targets over USB to the XIAO ESP32-S3. The 4 GB model is enough for the ROS 2 stack and keeps the logic power budget near 7 W typical.
pi5_4gb.role: Sits on M2.5 × 6 stand-offs on the electronics deck, fed from the 5 V regulator through GPIO pins 2/4 and 6/14.

pi5_cooler.summary: Official clip-on heatsink and PWM fan for the Raspberry Pi 5
pi5_cooler.description: Clip-on aluminium heatsink with a temperature-controlled fan that plugs into the Pi 5 fan header. Inside a closed shell the Pi would throttle under ROS 2 load; the cooler keeps it at full clock.
features: Fan speed controlled by the Pi firmware
pi5_cooler.role: Mounted on top of the Raspberry Pi 5 on the electronics deck.

microsd_64.summary: Fast A2 microSD card holding the Pi operating system and containers
microsd_64.description: The boot and root storage for the Raspberry Pi 5. The A2 application-performance class gives the random I/O that Docker images and ROS 2 logs need. Buy from retailer stock: fake cards are common.
features: 64 GB room for images and bags
microsd_64.role: Inserted in the Raspberry Pi 5 card slot.

camera_module_3_wide.summary: 12 MP wide-angle autofocus camera for the robot's face
camera_module_3_wide.description: Official Raspberry Pi camera with a Sony IMX708 sensor, autofocus and a wide lens. It looks forward from a printed tilt mount behind the front shell and feeds the Pi over MIPI CSI-2. The wide variant sees more of the floor right in front of the feet.
camera_module_3_wide.role: Held on the camera tilt plate at the front, cabled to the Pi 5 CAM port.

camera_cable_300.summary: 300 mm ribbon from the Pi 5 22-pin camera port to the 15-pin camera
camera_cable_300.description: The Pi 5 uses the smaller 22-pin (0.5 mm pitch) camera connector while the Camera Module 3 has the 15-pin standard connector. The 300 mm length reaches from the deck to the front camera through the shell slot.
camera_cable_300.role: Runs from the Pi 5 CAM port through the front-shell slot to the camera.

xiao_esp32s3.summary: Thumb-sized ESP32-S3 board running the real-time servo and sensor firmware
xiao_esp32s3.description: The motion controller of Strido. It receives joint targets from the Pi over USB, drives the PCA9685 over I²C at 400 kHz, reads the IMU and power monitor, and draws the face on the LCD over SPI. It was chosen for its tiny footprint and native USB.
xiao_esp32s3.role: Taped in the front cavity, powered and connected by USB from the Pi, master of the I²C bus.

pca9685.summary: 16-channel 12-bit PWM driver that generates all twelve servo pulses
pca9685.description: The PCA9685 creates the servo pulses in hardware so the ESP32 only writes registers over I²C. Strido runs it at 200 Hz with 500-2500 µs pulses on channels 4-15. Clones are fine if they keep the Adafruit 815 footprint.
features: Active-low OE for a safe start-up
pca9685.role: On the deck between the XIAO (I²C, OE) and the twelve servo signal leads.

lsm6dsox.summary: 6-axis accelerometer and gyroscope for body attitude
lsm6dsox.description: The IMU measures acceleration and rotation of the body so the controller can estimate tilt and balance. It sits in a pocket in the electronics deck near the centre of the robot and talks I²C at address 0x6A.
lsm6dsox.role: Pressed into the deck pocket and wired to the XIAO I²C bus.

ina260.summary: Current, voltage and power monitor with an integrated shunt
ina260.description: Measures the logic-branch current and the pack voltage so the robot can publish battery state and warn before the LiPo is over-discharged. The A0 jumper is bridged to move it to 0x41, away from the PCA9685.
ina260.role: In the logic branch between the logic fuse/switch and the 5 V regulator.

lcd_2inch.summary: 2-inch 240 × 320 IPS screen that shows the robot's face and status
lcd_2inch.description: A small SPI display behind a window in the front shell. The ESP32 drives it for an animated face and quick status without needing a monitor.
lcd_2inch.role: Behind the front shell window on the display bracket, wired to the XIAO SPI pins.

rplidar_c1.summary: 360° time-of-flight laser scanner for mapping and obstacle detection
rplidar_c1.description: The RPLIDAR C1 spins on top of the robot and returns a ring of distance points for SLAM and navigation in ROS 2. The genuine Slamtec unit is recommended because the official ROS driver supports it.
rplidar_c1.role: On the LiDAR pedestal on the top shell, USB to the Pi 5.

stemma_qt_female.summary: JST SH 4-pin to female jumper cable for the I²C sensors
stemma_qt_female.description: Adapts the IMU's STEMMA QT sockets to 0.1 in header pins: one cable from the PCA9685 header to the IMU (W18), one from the IMU to the INA260 header (W19). The IMU sits 2.5 mm under the Pi, where only this low plug fits. It carries 3.3 V, ground, SDA and SCL.
stemma_qt_female.role: W18 and W19, the I²C daisy chain PCA9685 → LSM6DSOX → INA260.

resistor_2k2.summary: Pull-up that keeps the servo outputs disabled while the controller boots
resistor_2k2.description: Holds the PCA9685 OE pin high (outputs off) until the firmware actively pulls it low, so servos cannot twitch at power-up or reset.
resistor_2k2.role: Soldered on the PCA9685 header between OE and VCC.

servo_spt5435lv.summary: 35 kg·cm 180° digital servo that drives each of the 12 joints
servo_spt5435lv.description: Every hip, thigh and knee joint is a SPT5435LV-180W servo. It gives high torque on 6 V at a low price and the 180° variant maps 500-2500 µs to the full joint range. Thirteen are ordered: twelve plus one spare.
servo_spt5435lv.role: Three per leg, signal from the PCA9685, power from the 6 V UBEC bus.

disc_horn_25t.summary: Aluminium 25-tooth disc horn for the hip and thigh joints
disc_horn_25t.description: A round metal horn that clamps on the servo spline and gives a wide bolt circle for the leg parts. Aluminium does not strip like the plastic horns supplied with most servos.
disc_horn_25t.role: Joins the femur and each leg module to its servo output.

arm_horn_25t.summary: Clamping aluminium arm horn for the knee drive
arm_horn_25t.description: A single-arm horn with a clamp screw that drives the knee linkage. The clamp stops backlash on the spline.
arm_horn_25t.role: On each knee servo, linked to the knee linkage with an M3 × 16 screw.

bearing_625zz.summary: Shielded 5 × 16 × 5 mm ball bearing for the hip pivot
bearing_625zz.description: Supports the outer end of each hip so the servo is not loaded sideways. Pressed into the outer shoulder frames.
bearing_625zz.role: In the outer shoulder frames, carrying the hip pivot screw.

bearing_6805.summary: Thin-section 25 × 37 × 7 mm sealed bearing for the knee crank
bearing_6805.description: A large thin bearing that lets the shoulder crank turn freely around the thigh axis while carrying the leg load.
bearing_6805.role: Pressed into the left/right shoulder crank, over the femur servo connector.

bearing_633zz.summary: Shielded 3 × 13 × 5 mm ball bearing for the knee joint
bearing_633zz.description: Two per leg in the tibia halves, giving a low-friction knee pivot on an M3 axle.
bearing_633zz.role: In the inner and outer tibia, on the knee axle.

sleeve_3x5x5.summary: Sintered bronze bushing for the linkage eyes
sleeve_3x5x5.description: Small oil-impregnated bushings pressed into each link eye so the M3 pins do not wear the plastic.
sleeve_3x5x5.role: Eight per leg in the long and short links.

ubec_10a.summary: 10 A switching regulator that powers six servos at 6.0 V
ubec_10a.description: Each UBEC steps the 2S pack down to 6.0 V for one pair of legs. Two units share the servo load so no single converter has to carry all twelve servos.
ubec_10a.role: Pack branch in, 6 V out to the front or rear WAGO servo bus.

lipo_2s_5000.summary: 7.4 V 5000 mAh hardcase LiPo that powers the whole robot
lipo_2s_5000.description: A two-cell lithium-polymer pack under the deck. It stores about 37 Wh and can deliver far more current than the servos need. The hardcase and the 138 × 47 × 25 mm limit match the battery bay.
lipo_2s_5000.role: Strapped under the deck, feeds the main fuse through W01.

charger.summary: Mains-powered balance charger for the LiPo pack
charger.description: Charges the 2S pack with cell balancing so no cell goes over 4.2 V.
charger.role: Bench equipment; connects to the pack's XT60 and balance lead.

lipo_bag.summary: Fire-resistant bag for charging and storing the LiPo
lipo_bag.description: Contains flames and sparks if a damaged pack fails during charging or storage.
lipo_bag.role: Bench safety equipment used while charging.

lipo_checker.summary: Cell voltage checker with low-voltage buzzer
lipo_checker.description: Shows each cell voltage on the balance lead and beeps before the pack is over-discharged.
lipo_checker.role: Plugs into the pack balance lead.

pololu_regulator.summary: 5 V 5.5 A step-down regulator for the Pi and logic
pololu_regulator.description: A high-efficiency buck regulator that feeds the Raspberry Pi 5 and USB devices. The Pi 5 needs a stiff 5 V; cheap buck modules often overstate their current.
pololu_regulator.role: On M2 stand-offs on the deck, between the INA260 and the Pi GPIO 5 V pins.

pololu_switch.summary: MOSFET soft power switch controlled by a pushbutton
pololu_switch.description: Switches the logic branch on and off with a small momentary button instead of a heavy toggle. It also gives reverse-voltage protection.
pololu_switch.role: Foam-taped on the deck, in the logic branch after the 7.5 A fuse.

pushbutton.summary: Stainless 12 mm momentary button for power on/off
pushbutton.description: The external power button in the back shell; it drives the Pololu switch A/B pads.
pushbutton.role: In the back shell, wired to the Pololu switch (W13).

xt60_pairs.summary: Genuine Amass XT60H connectors for battery lead, arming port and loop key
xt60_pairs.description: High-current power connectors. One pair joins the battery, one forms the rear arming port and one becomes the loop key that enables the servo branch.
xt60_pairs.role: Battery lead, rear arming port in the bezel, and the loop key.

fuse_holder.summary: Inline ATO blade-fuse holder with 14 AWG leads
fuse_holder.description: One holder protects the whole pack (25 A), the second the logic branch (7.5 A).
fuse_holder.role: Main fuse after the battery lead; logic fuse before the power switch.

fuse_25a.summary: 25 A blade fuse for the main battery line
fuse_25a.description: Blows before the 14 AWG main wiring overheats in a short circuit.

fuse_7_5a.summary: 7.5 A blade fuse for the logic branch
fuse_7_5a.description: Protects the 18 AWG logic wiring, switch and 5 V regulator.

wago_221_415.summary: Five-way lever connector for the servo power buses
wago_221_415.description: Tool-free splice blocks that distribute 6 V and ground to the servo leads; four per bus.
wago_221_415.role: Clipped into the front and rear servo-bus holders.

wire_14awg.summary: Flexible 14 AWG silicone wire for the main battery current
wire_14awg.description: Carries the full pack current from battery to fuse, arming port and UBECs.

wire_18awg.summary: 18 AWG silicone wire for UBEC outputs and the logic branch
wire_18awg.description: Sized for up to 10 A per UBEC output and the logic branch.
wire_18awg.role: Wires W04/logic, W05–W11 and W24 (1 m red + 1 m black per unit; two units).

wire_22awg.summary: Thin silicone wire for the Pi 5 V feed, button and jumpers
wire_22awg.description: Used in parallel pairs for the Pi 5 V feed and for low-current signals.
wire_22awg.role: W12 Pi feed, button wiring and jumpers.

usb_a_c_short.summary: 20 cm angled USB-A to USB-C cable
usb_a_c_short.description: Short angled cables for the Pi-to-XIAO and Pi-to-LiDAR adapter links in the tight body.
usb_a_c_short.role: Pi USB port to the XIAO and to the LiDAR USB adapter.

dupont_set.description: Jumpers for the bench set-up when centring the servos and testing the boards before they go into the robot.

heat_shrink.description: Insulates and strain-relieves every solder joint and splice.
heat_shrink.role: Over all soldered power and signal joints.

cable_ties.description: Tie the harness at every marked point of the routed wiring and hold the main fuse holder in the rear cavity.
cable_ties.role: Cable management and fuse holder mounting.

spiral_wrap.summary: Black spiral wrap for the cable bundles
spiral_wrap.description: Wraps every bundle of three or more cables where it passes a frame opening or runs near a moving part; the wiring check sizes the bundles and their length.
spiral_wrap.role: Protects the servo leads and power bundles in the cavities and openings.

cable_tie_mounts.summary: Small adhesive base for a cable tie
cable_tie_mounts.description: Two mounts on the deck side strips hold the logic and signal bundles beside the Pi and the PCA9685.
cable_tie_mounts.role: Tie points on the electronics deck.

dupont_crimp_contacts.summary: Loose Dupont contacts and housings for crimping
dupont_crimp_contacts.description: The servo signal wires, the I²C wires and the Pi 5 V feed are cut to length and get new female contacts in 1- to 4-pin housings; needs the Dupont crimp tool.
dupont_crimp_contacts.role: Signal connectors at the PCA9685 (servo signals, W17, W20) and the Pi header (W12, W22).

solder.description: For the XT60s, fuse holders, ground star, UBEC leads, switch terminals and the XIAO pins.
solder.role: Every soldered joint of the harness.

velcro.summary: Hook-and-loop strap that holds the battery
velcro.description: Holds the LiPo under the deck and allows quick removal for charging.

foam_tape.description: Mounts the XIAO, UBECs and power switch while damping vibration.
foam_tape.role: Under the XIAO, UBECs and Pololu switch.

m3_kit.summary: Stainless M3 socket head screw kit with nuts and washers
m3_kit.description: Covers most of the robot's M3 screws, nuts and washers in one box.

m3x10_100.summary: M3 × 10 socket head screws, the most-used screw in the robot
m3x10_100.description: Used for the frame, servo ears and shoulder frames; a 100-pack covers them all.

m3x20.description: Clamp the femur to its disc horn and close the servo mounts.
m3x20.role: Femur, servo mount top brackets and foot spacer.

m3_nyloc.summary: M3 nylon-insert lock nuts for moving joints
m3_nyloc.description: Hold their position on pivot screws that must stay just loose enough to turn.
m3_nyloc.role: Tibia, knee linkage and camera pivot.

m2_5x5.summary: M2.5 × 5 screws for boards and stand-offs
m2_5x5.description: Fix the stand-offs to the deck and the boards to the stand-offs.

m2_5x6.summary: M2.5 × 6 screws for the IMU, arming port and LiDAR
m2_5x6.description: Slightly longer M2.5 screws for parts with thicker clamps.
m2_5x6.role: IMU, arming port ring and RPLIDAR C1.

m2x5.summary: M2 × 5 screws for the regulator and display
m2x5.description: Small screws for the Pololu regulator stand-offs and the display bracket.

m2x10.description: Fix the Camera Module 3 to its tilt plate.

m2_nuts.description: Back the camera screws behind the tilt plate.

m2_5_nuts.description: Hold the IMU screws under the deck.
m2_5_nuts.role: IMU pocket in the electronics deck.

standoff_m2_5x6.description: Lift the Pi, PCA9685 and INA260 off the deck for airflow and wiring room.
standoff_m2_5x6.role: Under the Pi 5, PCA9685 and INA260.

standoff_m2x8.description: Raise the Pololu regulator above the deck.

threadlocker.description: Keeps metal-to-metal screws such as the horn centre screws from loosening under vibration while staying removable.
threadlocker.role: Servo horn centre screws and other metal threads.

filament_primary.summary: Graphite/black filament for the structural parts
filament_primary.description: Prints the frame, legs, brackets and mounts; about 1 kg covers the primary-colour parts.
features: PETG (the material the slicer profile and the strength check assume)

filament_secondary.summary: Lime/yellow filament for the shells and shoulders
filament_secondary.description: Prints the body shells and the shoulder cranks in the accent colour.
features: PETG (the material the slicer profile and the strength check assume)

pi_psu.summary: Official 27 W USB-C supply for bench work without the battery
pi_psu.description: Powers the Pi 5 at full USB current on the bench for software work, without arming the servos.
pi_psu.role: Bench supply into the Pi 5 USB-C port.

arming_port_bezel.summary: Rear bezel that holds the XT60 arming port
arming_port_bezel.description: Frames the XT60H arming port in the back shell; the ring clamps it from inside with two M2.5 × 6 screws.
arming_port_bezel.role: In the back shell, holding the servo arming port (Step 16).

arming_port_ring.summary: Clamp ring for the arming port
arming_port_ring.description: Clamps the bezel and XT60H from inside the back shell.
arming_port_ring.role: Inside the back shell behind the arming port bezel (Step 16).

back_shell_button.summary: Rear body shell with the 12 mm power-button hole
back_shell_button.description: Upstream back shell with the hole opened from 11.5 to 12.2 mm for the stainless button; it also carries the arming port.
back_shell_button.role: Closes the rear of the body (Step 16).

bottom_shell.summary: Belly shell that closes the battery bay
bottom_shell.description: Screws into the nuts of the lower shoulder frames with 8 × M3 × 8 and protects the battery.
features: 114 × 208 mm footprint needs a ≥ 220 mm bed

camera_mount_base.summary: Base with cheeks that carries the camera tilt pivot
camera_mount_base.description: Screws to the front upper shoulder frame with 2 × M3 × 12; the tilt plate hangs on an M3 × 40 pivot with a lock nut.
camera_mount_base.role: Front of the body, behind the front shell (Step 15).

camera_tilt_plate.summary: Plate that holds the Camera Module 3 at an adjustable tilt
camera_tilt_plate.description: The camera is fixed with 4 × M2 × 10 and nuts; friction on the pivot holds the 15° reference angle.
features: M2 holes for the camera board

display_bracket.summary: Flat bracket that clamps the LCD behind the front shell window
display_bracket.description: Fixed to the LCD studs with M2 × 5 and to the shell bosses with self-tapping M3 × 10.

electronics_deck.summary: Central plate that carries the boards and slides into the side beams
electronics_deck.description: Upstream plate extended with an IMU pocket and stand-off holes for the regulator and INA260. Stand-off screws sit in counterbores underneath.
features: Print top face down with supports
18 mm bridge over the IMU pocket
electronics_deck.role: Spine of the electronics, held in the side body beam grooves (Steps 1-2).

femur.summary: Thigh link that carries the knee
femur.description: Bolted to a disc horn on the thigh servo with 4 × M3 × 20; it bends under walking loads so print with solid walls.
features: Printed flat on its side with supports
femur.role: Between the thigh servo and the tibia (Step 9).

femur_servo_connector.summary: Hub that joins the femur to the thigh servo horn
femur_servo_connector.description: Clamped with the femur to the disc horn; the shoulder crank bearing turns on it.

foot_spacer.summary: Spacer clamped between the tibia halves at the foot
foot_spacer.description: Holds the two tibia halves at the right distance with an M3 × 20 screw and lock nut.

front_shell_display.summary: Front shell with display window and camera ribbon slot
front_shell_display.description: Upstream front shell with a 43 × 33 mm display window, two display bosses and a camera cable slot.
front_shell_display.role: Front of the body, with the LCD face (Step 14).

hip_bearing_pin.summary: Small pin that takes the hip pivot screw
hip_bearing_pin.description: Pressed into the leg servo mount; the M3 × 10 hip pivot screw passes through the 625 bearing into it.
hip_bearing_pin.role: Outer hip pivot of each leg (Steps 8, 13).

inner_shoulder_frame.summary: Bulkhead that holds the two hip servos
inner_shoulder_frame.description: Closes the frame with the side beams and carries the hip servos with M3 screws and nuts.

inner_tibia.summary: Inner half of the lower leg
inner_tibia.description: Paired with the outer tibia; holds a 633ZZ knee bearing.

left_servo_mount.summary: Leg servo mount for the rear-right leg
left_servo_mount.description: Holds the thigh and knee servos with 8 × M3 × 10; closed with the top bracket.

left_servo_mount_fl.summary: Front-left leg servo mount with hip pivot pilot
left_servo_mount_fl.description: Upstream left mount plus a 2.5 mm pilot for the front hip pivot.

left_shoulder.summary: Left knee drive crank with the 6805 bearing seat
left_shoulder.description: Turns on the 6805-2RS bearing around the thigh axis and drives the knee linkage.
left_shoulder.role: Knee drive on the FL and RL legs (Step 10).

lidar_pedestal.summary: Raised pedestal that holds the RPLIDAR C1 and its USB adapter
lidar_pedestal.description: Self-tapped to the top shell with 4 × M3 × 12; the LiDAR is fixed with 4 × M2.5 × 6.

stiff_long_link.summary: Strido long knee linkage rod, 10 mm wide in the leg plane
stiff_long_link.description: Transfers the knee servo's motion to the tibia. Same pin spacing (131 mm) and bushing eyes as the upstream Long_Link, but a 10 x 10 mm shaft instead of 5 x 8 mm, set 2 mm off the pin line away from the femur, so it no longer buckles when the knee servo stalls (ADR-010); sleeve-bearing pair in each eye.

lower_shoulder_frame_front.summary: Front lower shoulder frame with servo-bus pilot hole
lower_shoulder_frame_front.description: Upstream frame plus an M3 pilot for the front servo-bus holder; nut pockets for the bottom shell.

lower_shoulder_frame_rear.summary: Rear lower shoulder frame with servo-bus pilot hole
lower_shoulder_frame_rear.description: Same as the front version, for the rear servo-bus holder.

outer_shoulder_frame.summary: Outer frame with two 625ZZ hip bearing seats
outer_shoulder_frame.description: Supports the outer end of the hips through press-fit bearings.

outer_tibia.summary: Outer half of the lower leg
outer_tibia.description: Paired with the inner tibia; holds a 633ZZ knee bearing.

right_servo_mount.summary: Leg servo mount for the rear-left leg
right_servo_mount.description: Mirror of the left mount; holds thigh and knee servos.

right_servo_mount_fr.summary: Front-right leg servo mount with hip pivot pilot
right_servo_mount_fr.description: Upstream right mount plus a 2.5 mm pilot for the front hip pivot.

right_shoulder.summary: Right knee drive crank with the 6805 bearing seat
right_shoulder.description: Mirror of the left shoulder for the FR and RR legs.
right_shoulder.role: Knee drive on the FR and RR legs (Step 10).

servo_bus_holder_front.summary: Holder for four WAGO connectors of the front servo bus
servo_bus_holder_front.description: Self-taps to the front lower shoulder frame with one M3 × 12.

servo_bus_holder_rear.summary: Holder for four WAGO connectors of the rear servo bus
servo_bus_holder_rear.description: Self-taps to the rear lower shoulder frame with one M3 × 12.

servo_mount_top_bracket.summary: Bracket that closes each leg servo mount
servo_mount_top_bracket.description: Clamps both leg servos with 2 × M3 × 20.

short_link.description: Second linkage bar with bronze bushings.

side_body_beam.summary: Long side beam with the deck groove
side_body_beam.description: Holds the electronics deck in its groove and joins the shoulder frames.

top_shell_sensor.summary: Top shell with LiDAR pedestal holes and cable slot
top_shell_sensor.description: Upstream top shell plus holes for the LiDAR pedestal and a USB cable slot; closed with 6 × M3 × 8.

upper_shoulder_frame.summary: Upper shoulder frame with shell nut pockets
upper_shoulder_frame.description: Joins the shoulder frames and carries M3 nuts for the top shell and camera base.
